headline: OpenAI Ships Codex to Mobile App and Chrome Extension
raw_snippet: OpenAI sent a product update email on May 23 announcing Codex now works on mobile (iOS and Android) and in Chrome. Users can monitor active AI workflows, approve commands, launch tasks, and supervise coding agents remotely. The mobile app uses a secure relay layer that keeps trusted machines reachable across devices. Codex is available in preview across all plans including Free and Go tiers.

headline: OpenAI Named Leader in 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Enterprise AI Coding Agents
raw_snippet: OpenAI was named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Enterprise AI Coding Agents, with Codex recognized for innovation and enterprise-scale deployment. Gartner recognized Codex's strengths across agentic software development, enterprise governance, sandboxing, and flexible deployment options. Since Gartner's evaluation, OpenAI has introduced GPT-5.5, stronger tool use, and deeper enterprise software development workflow support. Codex is used by more than 4 million people weekly.

headline: OpenAI Confidentially Files S-1 IPO Prospectus with SEC, Targeting Q4 2026 Listing at Up to $1 Trillion
raw_snippet: OpenAI confidentially filed its S-1 IPO prospectus with the SEC on May 22, 2026, targeting a Q4 2026 public listing at a valuation between $852 billion and $1 trillion. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are co-leading the deal, with JPMorgan Chase also involved. The company is generating roughly $2 billion per month in revenue with an annualized run rate of $25 billion, but reported a negative 122% non-GAAP operating margin in Q1 2026. CEO Altman told staff that 'filing is different from being ready to go public.'

headline: ChatGPT Launches PowerPoint Add-In for AI-Powered Slide Creation and Editing
raw_snippet: OpenAI launched a ChatGPT add-in for Microsoft PowerPoint in beta, allowing users to create, edit, and update slides using AI-generated content. The add-in can ingest notes, documents, spreadsheets, images, and existing presentations and generate structured, editable slides. It also features advanced reasoning that can analyze a finished deck to identify narrative weak points and predict objections. Available to all ChatGPT tiers including Free, Go, Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu.

headline: OpenAI IPO Filing Reveals Negative 122% Operating Margin in Q1 2026 and $600B in Compute Commitments
raw_snippet: OpenAI's confidential S-1 filing reveals the company lost $1.22 for every $1 of revenue in Q1 2026 — a negative 122% non-GAAP operating margin, or roughly $6.95 billion in quarterly losses. The company is on the hook for approximately $600 billion in compute commitments over the next five years. OpenAI projects $14 billion in losses for full-year 2026 on $30 billion in revenue. CFO Sarah Friar has internally signaled the company is 'not ready' for a public listing, creating tension with CEO Altman's timeline.

headline: OpenAI Confidentially Files for IPO Amid Race with SpaceX and Anthropic for Trillion-Dollar Listings
raw_snippet: OpenAI filed its confidential draft registration statement with the SEC on May 22. Fortune notes the filing may finally answer big questions about the company's path to profitability, the structure of its nonprofit-to-PBC conversion, and governance. The IPO would be the largest technology IPO in history if OpenAI reaches its $1 trillion target valuation. Anthropic is reportedly aiming for its own IPO later in 2026, creating an unprecedented concentration of AI company listings.

headline: OpenAI Confidentially Files IPO Prospectus Amid 'Trio of Trillion Dollar IPOs' Wave
raw_snippet: The Information reported that OpenAI was planning to file its IPO prospectus within weeks, alongside SpaceX's S-1 filing, in what newsletter sources called a 'Trio of Trillion Dollar IPOs' alongside Anthropic's own planned listing. OpenAI's filing comes days after the Musk lawsuit verdict cleared a key legal obstacle. The company is valued at $852 billion by private investors and could reach $1 trillion at listing.

headline: ChatGPT PowerPoint Add-In Integrates with Outlook, Gmail, and SharePoint for Enterprise Slide Generation
raw_snippet: OpenAI's ChatGPT add-in for PowerPoint integrates with connected services including Gmail, Outlook, and SharePoint, enabling enterprises to generate slides from existing documents and communications. The beta is available to all tiers including Free users. OpenAI cautions that complex template, font, and chart handling may not yet be fully supported.

headline: OpenAI Becomes C2PA Conforming Generator and Integrates Google SynthID Watermarking for AI Content Provenance
raw_snippet: OpenAI became a C2PA Conforming Generator Product and integrated Google DeepMind's SynthID invisible watermarking into images generated by ChatGPT, Codex, and the API. SynthID embeds a pixel-level signal that survives screenshots and format changes. OpenAI also previewed a public verification tool that lets anyone check whether an image was generated using OpenAI tools. The multi-layered approach addresses the limitation that C2PA metadata can be stripped during file transformations.

headline: OpenAI Model Disproves 80-Year-Old Erdős Conjecture in Discrete Geometry with 125-Page Proof
raw_snippet: An internal general-purpose reasoning model at OpenAI autonomously disproved a central conjecture in discrete geometry first posed by Paul Erdős in 1946 — the unit distance problem asking for the maximum number of unit-distance pairs among n points in a plane. The model produced a 125-page proof using algebraic number theory (infinite class field towers and the Golod-Shafarevich theorem), identifying an infinite family of examples that provide a polynomial improvement over previous theories. The result was verified by external mathematicians.

headline: OpenAI Math Breakthrough Verified by External Mathematicians; AI Goes Beyond Being 'Just an Assistant'
raw_snippet: External mathematicians who verified OpenAI's AI-generated proof disproving the Erdős conjecture in discrete geometry said 'AI has gone beyond being just an assistant.' The result is significant because it was achieved by a general-purpose reasoning model rather than a system specifically trained for mathematics. The proof discovered a novel connection to algebraic number theory that human mathematicians had not previously explored for this problem.

headline: OpenAI and Dell Technologies Partner to Bring Codex to Hybrid and On-Premises Enterprise Environments
raw_snippet: OpenAI and Dell Technologies announced a multi-year collaboration to deploy Codex across hybrid and on-premises enterprise environments via the Dell AI Data Platform and Dell AI Factory. The deal is OpenAI's first explicit hybrid-and-on-prem enterprise distribution play, targeting financial services, healthcare, and government buyers that cannot send data to public cloud. Codex now has more than 4 million weekly developer users.

headline: OpenAI and Dell Codex Deal Targets Regulated Industries Barred from Public Cloud
raw_snippet: OpenAI and Dell Technologies' multi-year Codex enterprise partnership specifically targets financial services, healthcare, and government buyers that cannot send data to public cloud environments. The deal leverages the Dell AI Data Platform and Dell AI Factory, giving Codex access to organizations' on-premises data stores. Codex use has expanded beyond code generation into agentic workflows including context-gathering, reporting, lead qualification, and feedback routing.

headline: Jury Unanimously Dismisses All Claims in Musk v. OpenAI Lawsuit on Statute of Limitations
raw_snippet: A nine-member advisory jury in Oakland, California took less than 90 minutes to unanimously dismiss all claims in Elon Musk's lawsuit against Sam Altman, Greg Brockman, and OpenAI, finding that Musk was beyond the three-year statute of limitations when he filed in February 2024. Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers agreed and tossed the case. Musk had alleged the defendants 'stole a charity' and sought up to $150 billion in disgorgement. Musk's attorney Marc Toberoff said they plan to appeal to the Ninth Circuit.

headline: Musk v. OpenAI Verdict Clears Major IPO Obstacle; Musk Vows Ninth Circuit Appeal
raw_snippet: A jury took less than two hours to reject all of Elon Musk's claims against OpenAI, finding he missed the statute of limitations. Musk slammed the verdict as a 'technicality' and vowed to appeal. The dismissal removes a significant legal overhang that could have forced OpenAI and Microsoft to disgorge up to $150 billion. Legal analysts note the case previewed how antitrust issues will shape AI's future, even though antitrust wasn't in the complaint. The verdict clears the path for OpenAI's confidential IPO filing days later.
